instruction: Prepare the daily financing cash flow schedule for all dates in treasury_post. Return cash_day, receipts_cents, repayments_cents ordered by ISO cash_day ascending. Both output amounts are nonnegative magnitudes in cents. Positive postings are cash draws and negative postings are cash repayments. The treasury reporting rule permits net presentation only for facilities whose net_allowed flag is 1. For each such facility, offset its draws and repayments within the same day and classify the residual by its sign. For a facility flagged 0, present every draw and repayment gross. Then sum the classified magnitudes across facilities for the day. Include days on which both totals are zero. Facility codes are unique in facility_rule, each posting matches one rule, each row is a separate posting even if another row has the same values, and there are no nulls. Same-day posting order has no effect. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Choose the station's opening stock from the distinct feasible bike counts in stock_option. Apply every demand_pulse to inventory in pulse_no order. Pulse numbers run consecutively from 1 and there are at most seven. A negative bike_delta requests rentals and a positive value requests returns. Fulfill as many bikes as possible in each pulse, respecting zero inventory and the dock capacity on the single service_card. Unserved bikes leave the system immediately. Each unserved rental bike incurs the rental_points charge and each unserved return bike incurs the return_points charge. Minimize total penalty points, then choose the smaller opening stock. Inputs contain no nulls. Return one row with columns opening_bikes, closing_bikes, penalty_points, source_id, in that order, citing the service card used for capacity and scoring. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

rows: Four docks are open. Score two points per refused rental bike and one per refused return bike.

instruction: Choose an order for the three packaging inspections A, B and C that minimizes expected minutes until first detection, conditional on the package having a detectable defect. The scenario rows are mutually exclusive and their frequencies are relative counts. The detects string lists every inspection that would detect that scenario's defect. An empty string represents a defect-free package and is excluded when conditioning. Inspections run sequentially, each costs its full duration in minutes, and its result becomes available at completion. Stop at the first detection. Evaluate all six orders, accounting for which scenarios remain after earlier inspections miss. Return one row with inspection_order as three concatenated codes, then expected_minutes rounded to three decimal places. Choose using the unrounded expectation and break an exact tie by lexicographically smallest order. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Reserve storage for every wagon in the single manifest for one night. The two yards have codes E and W. For each yard, each tariff slip quotes the full price in cents for one exact block size in whole wagons. Only listed sizes can be booked, and exactly one slip per yard must be selected, including a zero-size slip for an unused yard. If both yards take wagons, add the manifest's one-time split handling charge. Minimize the total payable cents, then prefer more wagons at E. Slip IDs are unique, each yard and size has at most one slip, all fields are non-null, and an exact allocation exists. Return one row with ordered columns east_qty, west_qty, payable_cents, east_slip, west_slip. Cite both selected slips. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.
